Rashi on Shabbat 157a:10:1.hebrew: לצורך השבת - אלמא הפרת נדרים מעת לעת של שמיעה. הלכך, שלא לצורך לא, מדלא שרי אלא לצורך:
Rashi on Shabbat 157a:10:1.english: For the purpose of Shabbat - Apparently, the nullification of vows is [valid] for a twenty-four-hour period from [the time of] hearing [the vow]. Therefore, [when it is] not for the purpose [of Shabbat, it is] not [permitted], since it is only permitted for the purpose [of Shabbat].

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:11:1.hebrew: להקל ולהחמיר - כלומר, פעמים שיש שהות גדול, ופעמים שאינו אלא מעט:
Rashi on Shabbat 157a:11:1.english: To be lenient and to be strict - That is to say, sometimes there is a long period [of time], and sometimes it is only a short [while].

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:12:1.english: A dilemma was raised before them - [Regarding] that which [the Mishnah] teaches, "one may request [dissolution] for vows that are for [a Shabbat] need."

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:12:2.hebrew: כשלא היה לו פנאי - לשאל. מערב שבת קאמר, או אפילו כשהיה לו פנאי:
Rashi on Shabbat 157a:12:2.english: When he did not have time - to ask [for dissolution of the vow]. [Does] it mean [when he did not have time] before Shabbat, or even when he had time?

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:13:1.english: A small heilketei - A small path between two houses.

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:1:1.english: One may not chop wood from the beams - A stack of beams that are set aside and arranged for building.

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:1:2.hebrew: ולא מן קורה - הישנה שנשברה היום, ומהשתא להסקה קיימא, ואפ"ה אסור, הואיל ובין השמשות לא איתכן להכי:
Rashi on Shabbat 157a:1:2.english: Nor from a beam - The old one that broke today, and from now on it stands [ready] for firewood, and even so it is forbidden, since at twilight it was not prepared for this.

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:1:3.hebrew: מתחילין - להסיק בערימת התבן, קא סלקא דעתך בתיבנא סריא דסתמיה להסקה:
Rashi on Shabbat 157a:1:3.english: One may start - to kindle [a fire] with a pile of straw; it was initially assumed [that this refers] to spoiled straw, whose ordinary use is for fuel.

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:1:4.hebrew: אבל לא בעצים שבמוקצה - שהניחם ברחבה שאחורי ביתו, והקצם לימות הסתיו. מוקצה — רחבה שאחורי בתים, שהקצה אחורי ביתו להכניס שם דבר לאוצר:
Rashi on Shabbat 157a:1:4.english: But not with wood that is in the muktzeh - For he placed them in the open area behind his house and set them aside for the winter days. Muktzeh [means] an open area behind houses, where one set aside [the space] behind his house to bring things in there for storage.

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:1:5.english: With cedars and firs - Male cedar and female cedar, which are designated for building.

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:2:1.hebrew: משקין - אורחא דמילתא נקט, משום סירכא דמשכא שתהא נוחה להפשיט:
Rashi on Shabbat 157a:2:1.english: One gives water - [The Tanna] stated the usual practice, because of the adhesion of the hide, so that it will be easy to flay.

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:2:2.english: Desert [animals] - [Those] that always graze in the pasture and spend the night within the [Shabbat] boundary.

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:3:1.english: Another unattributed [mishna] - Beit Hillel is considered like an unattributed [mishna].

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:4:1.hebrew: כל הכלים ניטלין - ואפי' מלאכתן לאיסור, ורבי שמעון היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 157a:4:1.english: All vessels may be moved - Even [those whose] use is for a forbidden [purpose], and [this Mishnah] is [in accordance with] Rabbi Shimon.

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:4:2.hebrew: חוץ מן המסר הגדול - מגירה שהיא לאומנין לקוץ בה עצים. ומוקצה מחמת חסרון כיס הוא, שלא ישתברו חריצים, שהוא עשוי כסכין מלא פגימות:
Rashi on Shabbat 157a:4:2.english: Except for the large saw - A saw belonging to craftsmen for cutting wood. And it is muktzeh due to monetary loss, so that [its] teeth do not break, for it is made like a knife full of notches.

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:4:3.hebrew: ויתד של מחרישה - החופר את הקרקע, קולטר"א בלע"ז:
Rashi on Shabbat 157a:4:3.english: And the blade of a plow - [That] which digs the earth, coltre [coulter] in Old French.

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:5:1.english: They may nullify - [A] husband [may nullify vows] for his wife.

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:5:10.english: And [one may] measure - [in order] to ascertain a matter of halakhic ruling.

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:5:11.english: And tie - [One may tie] a knot that is not permanent, even initially.

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:5:2.english: And one may request - From a Sage.

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:5:3.english: That are for the purpose of Shabbat - For example, where one vowed not to eat today.

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:5:4.english: And one may seal the window - [This is] in accordance with the Rabbis, who say (above, Shabbat 125b): "One may seal [a window with] a window shutter."

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:5:5.hebrew: ומודדין את המקוה - במדה, שיהא שם עמוק שלש אמות מים, ורוחב אמה על אמה:
Rashi on Shabbat 157a:5:5.english: And one may measure a ritual bath - with a measure, [to see] that there is a depth of three cubits of water and a width of a cubit by a cubit.

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:5:6.hebrew: ואת המטלית - שתהא שלש על שלש אצבעות, כגון אם היתה טמאה ונגעה בטהרות:
Rashi on Shabbat 157a:5:6.english: And the rag - [To see] whether it is three by three fingerbreadths, for example, if it was ritually impure and touched ritually pure [items].

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:5:7.hebrew: בטפיח - פך של חרס, וחבירו בפי"ז (דף קכה:): זמורה שהיא קשורה בטפיח ממלאין בה בשבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 157a:5:7.english: With a tafiach - An earthenware jug; and its counterpart [appears] in Chapter 17 (125b): "A vine branch that is tied to a tafiach — one may draw [water] with it on Shabbat."

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:5:9.english: To know whether there is an opening of a handbreadth in the tub - It is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:6:1.hebrew: איבעיא להו הפרה - דמתניתין, בין לצורך [בין שלא לצורך] השבת, דגבי הפרה ביום שמעו כתיב (במדבר ל׳:ו׳), ואם לא מיפר האידנא, שוב אינו מיפר:
Rashi on Shabbat 157a:6:1.english: A dilemma was raised before them: Nullification - [that] of our Mishnah, whether for the need [or not for the need] of Shabbat. For regarding nullification, "on the day he hears" is written (Numbers 30:6), and if he does not nullify [it] today, he can no longer nullify [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:6:2.hebrew: ושאלה לצורך אין, שלא לצורך לא - דיכול לישאל למחר, ומשום הכי מפליג להו מהדדי, ולא קתני מפירין ונשאלין לנדרים שהן לצורך השבת, דלא קאי לצורך אלא אשאלה:
Rashi on Shabbat 157a:6:2.english: And requesting [dissolution] for the purpose [of Shabbat], yes; not for the purpose [of Shabbat], no - Because one can request [dissolution] tomorrow [after Shabbat], and therefore [the Tanna] separates them from each other and does not teach, "One may nullify and request [dissolution] for vows that are for the purpose of Shabbat," because [the phrase] "for the purpose [of Shabbat]" refers only to requesting [dissolution].

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:9:1.hebrew: הכי גרסי' ל"א איבעיא להו (במסכת נדרים דף עז.) לצורך אתרוייהו קאי - אהפרה ואשאלה, אבל הפרה שלא לצורך — לא. אלמא הפרת נדרים מעת לעת, וזה ששמע בשבת יכול להפר משתחשך בתוך מעת לעת של שמיעה; הלכך שלא לצורך לא שרינן בשבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 157a:9:1.english: Thus we read [the text]: "Another version: it was asked of them (in Tractate Nedarim, 77a): 'For the purpose [of Shabbat]' refers to both of them" - To nullification [of a vow] and to absolution [from a vow], but nullification not for the purpose [of Shabbat] — no [it is not permitted]. Apparently, nullification of vows [may be performed] for a twenty-four hour period [from when the vow is heard], and one who heard [a vow] on Shabbat can nullify [it] after dark, within the twenty-four hour period of hearing [it]; therefore, [when it is] not for the purpose [of Shabbat], we do not permit [it] on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 157a:9:2.hebrew: כל היום - עד שתחשך ותו לא, ואפילו שמע סמוך לחשיכה. הלכך, אפי' שלא לצורך, שאם לא יפר עכשיו לא יפר עוד:
Rashi on Shabbat 157a:9:2.english: All day - Until it gets dark, and no more, even if he heard [the vow] close to nightfall. Therefore, [he may nullify it] even [when it is] not for [the] need [of Shabbat], for if he does not nullify [it] now, he will not [be able to] nullify [it] any longer.

Tosafot on Shabbat 157a:11:1.hebrew: והלכתא מעת לעת - לא גרס בפירוש ר"ח, דבנדרים משמע דלית הלכתא הכי, דאמר בפרק נערה המאורסה (כתובות דף עו:): אין הלכה כאותו הזוג. מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 157a:11:1.english: And the halakhah is [that he may nullify] for a twenty-four-hour period - This reading does not appear in the commentary of Rabbeinu Chananel, for in [Tractate] Nedarim it is implied that the halakhah is not like this, as it states in the chapter [entitled] Na'arah HaMe'orasah (Ketubot 76b): "The halakhah is not in accordance with that pair." [This was taught] by our master.

Tosafot on Shabbat 157a:13:1.hebrew: הלקטי קטנה - מפרש בקונטרס: שביל קטן היתה בין שני בתים, והגיגית סדוקה מונחת על גבן, והמת מוטל בהלקטי תחת הגיגית נגד הסדק, וקשרו המקידה לידע אם יש בסדק פותח טפח. ולהאי פירושא קשה לר"י: דאפי' אין בסדק פותח טפח, כיון שהמת נגדו, לא חשבינן לה כמאהיל על המת, כיון שאין [זה] דרך מאהיל, כדמוכח במסכת אהלות (פ"י מ"ה) ומייתי לה בסוף פרק קמא דסוכה (דף יח. ושם): "אין בארובה פותח טפח והמת בבית — מה שבבית כנגד ארובה טהור; המת כנגד ארובה — מה שבבית טהור". וכיון שהמת היה נגד הסדק, מה היה להם לקשור המקודה? ועוד פירש, שלפני מות המת פקקו המאור בטפיח. ולא הבין רבי לפירושו: הלא אותו מת לא היה מת שלם, שהרי לא ידעו אם למעלה הימנו היה פותח טפח, והמת היה כולו תחת הסדק! אלא ודאי כזית מן המת היה; וא"כ לא היה לו לומר "לפני מות המת", אלא "לפני שבא כזית מן המת לשם". ומיהו יתכן לומר, שהמת היה כולו מוטל תחת הגיגית שלא כנגד הסדק, והגיגית היתה סדוקה באמצע מראשה לסופה; ואילו היה באותו סדק על פני כולו פותח טפח, לא היתה טומאה עוברת, דלא חשיב כאהל אחד, אבל אין בו פותח טפח — כאלו אין כאן סדק וחשיב כאהל אחד, ומביא את הטומאה לבית. וקושיא ראשונה מכל מקום במקומה עומדת. ונראה כפירוש ר"ח, דמפרש דהלקטי היינו תל המתלקט, ואותה הלקטי היתה בין שני בתים, והמת היה בבית אחד, ואותה הגיגית היתה למעלה מן התל עד לתקרה, ואותה הגיגית לא היתה טמאה, שהרי בטלה שם; ואם לא היתה סדוקה, לא היה הבית אחר טמא, אלא הגיגית היתה סדוקה מצדה. והשתא אתי שפיר דקתני "סדוקה", לפי שהיא מצדה; אבל לפירוש הקונטרס לא אתי שפיר, דכיון דפירש שהסדק למעלה מן הגיגית, היה לו לומר "פתוחה" ולא "סדוקה", אבל לפר"ח אתי שפיר, שהסדק היה מן הצד, וקשרו את המקידה לידע אם יש פותח טפח. ויש לנו לומר שאותו חור היה עשוי לתשמיש, דחור העשוי לתשמיש שיעורו בפותח טפח; ואם היה פותח טפח, הבית אחר טמא, ואם לאו — טהור. ומיהו קשה לר"י לפירוש ר"ח, דלא הוה ליה למימר "על גבן", אלא "על גבה". מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 157a:13:1.english: A small alleyway [heilketei] - Rashi (haKuntres) explains: There was a small path between two houses, and a cracked tub was placed on top of them, and the corpse was lying in the heilketei under the tub opposite the crack, and they tied the earthenware shard [mekidah] to know whether there was an opening of a handbreadth in the crack. And according to this explanation, the Ri has a difficulty: for even if there is not an opening of a handbreadth in the crack, since the corpse is opposite it, we do not consider it as overshadowing the corpse, since this is not the manner of overshadowing — as is proven in Tractate Ohalot (10:5), and [the Gemara] cites it at the end of the first chapter of Sukkah (18a and there): "[If] there is not an opening of a handbreadth in a skylight, and the corpse is in the house — whatever is in the house opposite the skylight is pure; [if] the corpse is opposite the skylight — whatever is in the house is pure." And since the corpse was opposite the crack, why did they need to tie the mekudah? Furthermore, [Rashi] explained that before the dying person died, they sealed the window with an earthenware vessel. And my teacher did not understand his explanation: surely that corpse was not a whole corpse, for they did not know whether above it there was an opening of a handbreadth, and the entire corpse was under the crack! Rather, it was certainly an olive-sized piece of a corpse; and if so, [Rashi] should not have said "before the dying person died," but rather "before an olive-sized piece of a corpse came there." However, it is possible to say that the entire corpse was lying under the tub, not opposite the crack, and the tub was cracked in the middle from one end to the other; and if there had been an opening of a handbreadth in that crack along its entire length, the impurity would not pass through, as it would not be considered one tent, whereas [if] it does not have an opening of a handbreadth, it is as if there is no crack here and it is considered one tent, and it brings the impurity into the house. Nevertheless, the first difficulty still stands. Rather, it appears like the explanation of Rabbeinu Chananel, who explains that heilketei means a gathered mound [tel hamitlaktet], and that heilketei was between two houses, and the corpse was in one house, and that tub was above the mound up to the ceiling, and that tub was not susceptible to impurity, for it had been nullified there; and if it had not been cracked, the other house would not be impure — rather, the tub was cracked on its side. Now it fits well that [the Mishnah] teaches "cracked," because it is on its side; whereas according to Rashi's explanation it does not fit well, for since he explained that the crack was on top of the tub, it should have said "open" rather than "cracked," whereas according to Rabbeinu Chananel's explanation it fits well, for the crack was on the side, and they tied the mekidah to know if there was an opening of a handbreadth. And we must say that that hole was made for use, for a hole made for use has its minimum measure of an opening of a handbreadth; and if there was an opening of a handbreadth, the other house is impure, and if not, it is pure. However, the Ri has a difficulty with Rabbeinu Chananel's explanation: for [the Gemara] should not have said "on top of them" [al gaban], but rather "on top of it" [al gabah]. [From my teacher.]

Tosafot on Shabbat 157a:2:1.hebrew: אין משקין ושוחטין את המדבריות - הוה מצי למימר דהני כגרוגרות וצמוקין דמיין, כדאמר בפרק כירה (לעיל שבת דף מה:):
Tosafot on Shabbat 157a:2:1.english: One may neither give water to nor slaughter desert [animals] - [The Gemara] could have said that these are comparable to dried figs and raisins, as it says in the chapter [entitled] Kirah (above, Shabbat 45b).

Tosafot on Shabbat 157a:4:1.hebrew: לבר ממוקצה מחמת איסור - וכגון איסור דדחייה בידים, כגון נר שהדליקו באותו שבת, כדפירשתי בפ"ק בסופו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 157a:4:1.english: Except for [that which is] set aside due to prohibition - And [this refers to], for example, a prohibition of actively pushing [it] away with [one's] hands, such as a lamp that one kindled on that Shabbat, as I explained at the end of the first chapter.
